## The path from a missed due date to a single, targeted alert

**What starts the check.** Two independent triggers converge on the same job. The first is a plain HTTP cron endpoint, `POST /api/cron/overdue` (`src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`), guarded by `assertCronSecret` (`src/app/api/_lib/responses.ts`), which checks an `x-taskflow-cron` header against `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET` — this is meant to be hit by an external scheduler (e.g. Vercel Cron), and there's no `vercel.json` in the repo pinning the actual cadence. The second is an in-process fallback: `startScheduler()` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`, wired up once at boot from `src/instrumentation.ts`, runs a `setInterval` every 60s (`TICK_INTERVAL_MS`), and `tick(now)` checks `CADENCE_MINUTES["overdue-issues"] = 60` to decide whether it's due, then `enqueue`s and `drain`s the job via `src/server/jobs/queue.ts`'s `runHandler`. Both paths ultimately call `runOverdueIssueJob(now)` in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`.

**Narrowing the candidate set.** The actual filtering lives in `listOverdueIssues(orgId, now)` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` (~line 507). It queries the `issues` table per organization for rows where `dueAt` is not null and `dueAt < now`, status is one of `backlog`/`todo`/`in_progress`/`in_review` (excluding completed/closed states), and the issue isn't archived (`livePredicate`). The job iterates orgs from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup()` (a helper repurposed from usage-rollup code) and runs this query once per org.

**What the detector does and doesn't own.** `runOverdueIssueJob` explicitly limits its responsibility, per its own comment: it announces the fact and delegates everything else. For each overdue issue not already reported, it calls `emit("issue.overdue", { orgId, issueId, dueAt, assigneeId, ... })` on the event bus (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`). It never writes a notification, never touches user preferences, never sends email — that's left entirely to whatever subscribes to the event.

**Stopping repeat announcements.** Deduplication happens inside the job itself via a module-level `Set<string>` called `reported` (`src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`, lines ~24–33): before emitting, it checks `if (reported.has(issue.id)) continue;`, and only adds the id after a successful `emit`. Notably, this is in-memory only — there's no `overdueNotifiedAt` column or dedupe table backing it, so a process restart clears `reported` and the next sweep will re-announce every still-overdue issue. The downstream notification insert has no unique constraint either, so this in-memory set is the sole guard against repeats within a running process.

**Reaching one specific person.** The only subscriber to `issue.overdue` is registered in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` (~lines 193–201), wired up at boot when `event-registry.ts` imports the module. It guards on `assigneeId === null` (unassigned issues are skipped), then calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], {...})`. `notify()` (same file, ~lines 46–89) loads that user's `NotificationPreference` row via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, kind)`, then calls `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` (~lines 156–171), which turns the user's `inApp`/`email`/`digestOnly` booleans into a channel list (defaulting to `["in_app", "email"]` if no preference exists) — if the user has muted everything, no row is written at all. The result is bulk-inserted via `notificationRepo.insertNotifications`.

Delivery then splits by channel: `in_app` is immediately visible through `listNotifications`/`countUnread`, surfaced in `notification-bell.tsx` and the notifications panel route. `email` is not sent immediately for this event type — it's only picked up later by the separate `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`), which runs on its own hourly-gated cadence per org, bundles unread notifications for `digestOnly` subscribers, renders and "sends" via `email-service.ts` (which just logs rather than calling a real transport), and marks those notifications read so the digest doesn't resend them. There's no Slack or push channel — `NotificationChannel` only supports `in_app`, `email`, and `webhook`, and webhook delivery is a separate, unrelated subscriber tree.
